Work-family crowding is the catalogue-wide count of books sharing the same work-family key.
The market-lift review group is built from the union of the initial quiet-praise review set and the companion early-contrast set, deduplicated by book id. Tension is market-lift percentile plus one minus lead-contributor-support percentile plus work-family-crowding percentile, with all three percentiles computed inside the finalized market-lift review group. Calculations use unrounded values. Report decimal-valued final results rounded to 4 decimal places. Shares are 0-1 ratios.

context: Use the Netflix catalog as a content strategy workspace, so start from a clean retained catalog. Parse date_added, leave invalid dates missing, extract movie minutes and show seasons from duration, and create a lowercase title key after trimming and collapsing whitespace. Keep records with usable title, type, release year, listed categories, and valid duration semantics; drop rows whose duration cannot be read for their type. For the opening view, use the stored country phrase as the market, fill missing country with Unknown, and assign each title to its first listed category. Fill missing descriptions with empty text. Count description words as whitespace-delimited tokens using Python-style str(description).split() on that filled text; do not strip punctuation, remove symbols, or use regex word-boundary tokenization before counting. Mark weak descriptions at or below the cleaned catalog's lower quartile of those token counts. Unless a later step narrows the denominator, market-category percentages use distinct retained catalog entries assigned to that cell. Shares enter formulas as 0 to 1 values, while reported percentages use a 0 to 100 scale. Use arithmetic means and linear-interpolated percentiles unless another aggregation is stated. Ranks are 1-based after the stated sort, with unresolved ties left in the current working order. Title counts always mean distinct retained catalog entries under the current assignment, not deduplicated title keys. The opening pressure score keeps cells with at least 15 titles and combines min-max scaled log title count at 44%, weak-description share at 31%, and strict higher-maturity share at 25%; strict higher maturity means TV-MA, R, or NC-17. Compute derived values with unrounded numbers and round final decimal outputs to 3 decimals.
question: After this cleanup, which five market-category niches have the strongest opening mix of supply pressure and weak discoverability? Report market, category, score, title count, weak-description percentage, and strict higher-maturity percentage.

context: The opening view treated a multi-country value as one market phrase. Now split comma-separated countries, trim spaces, and keep Unknown when no country is available. Keep the ten strongest split-market cells as the comparison slate. To see which opening leaders survive, compare each opening market phrase and category exactly as previously displayed, and count it only if the same pair remains in that ten-cell slate.
question: After co-produced titles are credited to each participating market, which opening leaders remain in the comparison slate, and which five non-opening niches become the strongest challengers? Report scores and title counts for both groups.

context: Keep the co-production market treatment and recast similar movie and television category labels so comparable audience promises are evaluated together. Give every listed category attached to a title credit after cleaning, and count duplicate cleaned labels inside the same title-market cell once. Recast categories this way: International TV Shows and International Movies become International; TV Dramas and Dramas become Dramas; TV Comedies and Comedies become Comedies; TV Action & Adventure and Action & Adventure become Action & Adventure; Crime TV Shows becomes Crime; Romantic TV Shows and Romantic Movies become Romantic; Kids' TV and Children & Family Movies become Kids & Family; Docuseries and Documentaries become Documentaries; Science & Nature TV becomes Science & Nature; Classic & Cult TV, Classic Movies, and Cult Movies become Classic & Cult; TV Horror and Horror Movies become Horror; Anime Series and Anime Features become Anime; Stand-Up Comedy and Stand-Up Comedy & Talk Shows become Stand-Up & Talk; TV Sci-Fi & Fantasy and Sci-Fi & Fantasy become Sci-Fi & Fantasy; LGBTQ Movies becomes LGBTQ; Spanish-Language TV Shows becomes Spanish-Language; Korean TV Shows becomes Korean; British TV Shows becomes British; Independent Movies becomes Independent; Music & Musicals becomes Music; TV Mysteries becomes Mysteries; TV Thrillers and Thrillers become Thrillers. Other cleaned labels remain as fine categories. Use cells with at least 18 titles. The previous split-market slate stays in its old displayed wording for comparison, so a renamed category is treated as absent under the old wording when rank movement is measured. Old-wording cells that no longer appear are placed one position after the last cleaned-category rank.
question: After category cleanup, which five earlier strong niches lose the most rank, and which five cleaned niches are the strongest risk candidates? Report both lists, and report rank movement for both lists. For the strongest cleaned risk candidates, compute rank movement as cleaned rank minus the previous split-market top-ten rank when the exact same market-category wording appeared in the previous slate; otherwise report rank movement as null.

context: Broaden audience risk from the strict adult labels to a teen-and-adult caution signal. Count TV-MA, R, NC-17, TV-14, and PG-13 as the broader risk group, with the risk percentage still using retained titles in the displayed niche as the denominator. Compare the ten-cell leading group under this broader reading with the immediately preceding strict-risk cleaned slate. Score movement is the broader-risk pressure score minus the strict-risk pressure score for the same market-category cell. First compare the strict-risk and broader-risk top-ten sets. If they have true entries or exits, report those groups. If there are no true entries or exits, report the five shared leaders with the largest score movements as gains and the five shared leaders with the smallest score movements as losses, even when all movements are positive.
question: With the broader audience-risk reading, which cleaned market-category niches enter or leave the ten-cell leading group compared with the previous strict-risk slate? Report five entries or largest gains and five exits or largest losses with their score movements.

context: As a sensitivity check, keep the broader audience-risk reading but return temporarily to the early market phrase and first-category wording. Use the original 15-title floor from that early view and compare only against the ten cleaned-risk leaders just established. Measure cleaning-path dependence as sensitivity rank minus current rank. If a leader is absent from the sensitivity view, place it after the last ranked cell before computing the penalty. Robust cases are present in the sensitivity view with the smallest penalty. Treat this as a read on whether the current leaders depend on the cleaning path.
question: Under that sensitivity view, which five current leading niches look most dependent on the cleaning path, and which five still look robust? Report the most fragile and most robust cases.

context: Return to the main cleaned market-category view and read freshness against the ten cleaned-risk leaders after the sensitivity check. Carry each leader's cleaning-dependence penalty forward: positive penalties reduce the freshness gap by dividing by one plus the penalty divided by 100, while negative penalties are treated as zero. Treat a title as fresh when its release year is 2018 or later, and calculate freshness percentage over retained assigned titles in the displayed niche. Catalog lag is parsed add-year minus release year, with missing parsed dates excluded from the lag average. The new-content gap multiplies the current pressure score by the non-fresh share and by one plus average platform lag divided by ten, then applies the penalty. Keep the ten highest gap-ranked cells as the shortlist for market support checks.
question: Among the cleaned high-pressure leaders carried out of the sensitivity read, which five show the clearest new-content gap? Report niche, freshness percentage, average platform lag over titles with parsed add dates, pressure score, and gap score.

context: Focus the market universe on countries with enough catalog support for a portfolio decision. Use the distribution of distinct retained catalog-entry counts created by the co-production market treatment, and keep markets at or above the 65th percentile of that support distribution with linear interpolation. Carry the ten gap-ranked niches from the freshness step into this check.
question: After applying the market support requirement, which five high-potential niches remain strongest and which five previously attractive niches are excluded? If no high-potential niche is excluded, report the five strongest surviving niches.

context: To check whether averages are overstating uneven cells, rerank the eligible-market shortlist with medians. Keep the same eligible markets, cleaned fine categories, broad audience risk, and 18-title floor, but use medians for the cell summaries before applying the same pressure structure. The median pressure ranking uses the support scale, median weak-description flag, and median broad-risk flag; title count remains a distinct retained catalog-entry count. Review the first eight surviving cells from the market-supported gap list. Each row's prior standing is its position in that eight-cell review list. Stable members are reviewed rows that still sit in the median-ranked top ten. Rank-loss cases are the reviewed rows with the largest loss. Return to the mean-based view afterward.
question: With median aggregation inside the eligible niches, which five shortlist members still sit in the median top ten and which five lose the most standing? Report the stable members and the largest rank losses.

context: Return to the main eligible-market path. Broaden the next shortlist back to the full broad-risk pressure table in supported markets, with the same cleaned-category treatment and 18-title floor. Carry the freshness gap where it exists from the freshness and market-support gap table. Keep the ten highest text-risk cells as the shortlist for the quality checks. Text notes are only a discoverability diagnosis for that shortlist. The text risk score multiplies the current pressure score by 0.65 plus weak-description share and by one plus the carried new-content gap, using zero when the gap is unavailable. Weak-description share uses retained assigned titles in each displayed niche as its denominator.
question: Which eligible high-pressure niches combine strong potential with the weakest description signals? Report the five most concerning cases with text risk, current pressure score, and title count.

context: Check quality first for the ten niches already under consideration, using the external IMDb data to test coverage and bias in the current text-risk shortlist. Use the IMDb movies displayed title column for title fields, ignoring original-title for this connection, and align the IMDb ratings file to it by original row position for weighted vote and vote-count fields. After this rowwise pairing, drop rows without a displayed title or weighted vote. Match Netflix and IMDb titles with the lowercase whitespace-normalized title key from the initial cleanup. When IMDb has multiple rows for a key, keep the row with the largest vote count. Treat a niche as having rating evidence when at least three titles are matched.
question: Using that first title connection to IMDb, which current shortlist niches have enough rating evidence to support the opportunity story, and which look under-covered with fewer than three matched titles? Report both groups with match counts and match percentages over retained titles in the niche; include average IMDb rating for supported niches and title count for under-covered niches.

context: Some coverage gaps come from title formatting, not true absence in IMDb. Clean title keys more aggressively by lowercasing, removing parenthetical fragments, replacing punctuation with spaces, removing the articles a, an, and the, and collapsing whitespace. Compare the evidence change for the same ten-niche shortlist. Newly matched titles are the clean-match count minus the earlier whitespace-match count. Match-percentage gain is the clean match percentage minus the earlier whitespace match percentage. Both percentages use retained Netflix catalog entries in the same shortlist niche as the denominator, not normalized title keys. When several IMDb rows share the cleaned key, keep the row with the largest vote count.
question: After the cleaner title connection, which five shortlist niches gain the most IMDb evidence? Report newly matched title count, match-percentage gain, clean matched-title count, and average IMDb rating.

context: Use the cleaner title connection as the active quality evidence and limit the quality read to the current ten text-risk shortlisted niches. Keep niches with at least three matched IMDb titles, then rank quality-backed candidates by multiplying text-risk score, mean IMDb rating divided by ten, and one-half plus match share. Match share is matched IMDb titles divided by retained Netflix catalog entries in the same niche, not normalized title keys.
question: Which niches now satisfy the current opportunity gates and show the strongest IMDb quality? Report the five strongest quality-backed candidates with quality score, average IMDb rating, matched-title count, and match share.

context: To keep a niche with only a few low-vote IMDb matches from dominating the slate, keep the same title connection and candidate set, and use the rowwise IMDb movies-plus-ratings pairing already established. Adjust each IMDb rating toward the global mean of the paired table's weighted vote over usable rows, using the median vote count from the same paired table as prior support. The adjusted rating is the sum of votes times rating and prior votes times global mean, divided by the sum of votes and prior votes. Recheck the quality-backed candidates with the same match-count requirement and compare the new five-cell leading group with the previous quality-backed group.
question: After applying the vote-support quality adjustment, which quality-backed candidates move into or out of that five-cell leading group? Report the entries with adjusted scores and the exits.

context: Separate title-key cleaning from the vote-support adjustment. Return to the earlier lowercase whitespace title connection but keep the adjusted quality reading based on vote support. Compare every candidate in the current adjusted-quality pool, not only the top five already shown, with that older connection by matched-title loss and adjusted-rating gap. Select sensitive cases by sorting by matched-title loss descending, then adjusted-rating gap descending. The hold-up group must still have at least three earlier-connection matches; sort hold-up cases by earlier-connection adjusted rating descending, then current adjusted quality score descending.
question: Which five current adjusted-quality candidates are most sensitive to the cleaner title connection, and which five still hold up under the earlier connection? Report both groups with the relevant match counts, rating gaps, and adjusted scores.

context: For a vote-tail sensitivity check, reduce the influence of extreme IMDb vote counts while keeping the cleaner title connection and the full current adjusted-quality pool. Dampened votes are clipped to the 5th and 95th percentiles of total votes from the paired IMDb table used for the vote-support adjustment, then the same adjustment is applied. Use linear interpolation for those percentiles. A candidate is stable when it still has at least three matches and its adjusted rating changes by no more than 0.15. Loss cases are those with the most negative dampened-minus-current adjusted-rating gap.
question: When extreme vote counts are dampened, which five adjusted-quality candidates remain stable and which five lose the most support by the winsorized-rating gap? Report both groups.

context: Return to the main vote-support quality reading. Add the book-adaptation signal only to explain the current quality candidates: match Goodreads original titles with the cleaned title key, keep the highest-ratings-count book for duplicate keys, and compute each niche's adaptation lift from the niche's mean Goodreads rating scaled to a ten-point range minus the niche's adjusted IMDb rating, multiplied by the natural log of one plus the niche's mean Goodreads rating volume and divided by ten. Missing book evidence contributes zero lift. Select support cases by sorting by book-match count descending, then adaptation lift descending. Select caution cases from niches with at least one book match by sorting adaptation lift ascending.
question: Among the current quality candidates, which five niches gain the clearest book-adaptation support and which five look most likely to be overstated by that support? Report the strongest support cases and the most cautionary cases.

context: Some title matches still miss stories because series markers, subtitles, and spacing differ across sources. Use a compact title key by lowercasing, cutting off text at the first colon or the first standalone marker word season, series, volume, vol, or book, then removing parenthetical fragments, punctuation, articles a, an, and the, and spaces. For IMDb, build that key from the same displayed title field used by the first IMDb connection, not the original-title field. For the book data, build it from Goodreads original titles and drop books without an original title. For duplicate compact keys, keep the IMDb row with the largest vote count and the book row with the largest ratings count. Refresh the cross-source quality reading for the ten text-risk niches used in the IMDb checks: combine adjusted IMDb quality divided by ten at 68%, Goodreads average rating multiplied by two and divided by ten at 22%, and Goodreads volume at 10%, where the volume ingredient is log1p of the niche's mean Goodreads ratings count divided by log1p of the maximum ratings count in the book table. Then multiply by text risk and one-half plus IMDb match share, where the share is a 0 to 1 value using retained Netflix catalog entries in the displayed niche as the denominator. Missing IMDb quality falls back to the global IMDb mean, while missing Goodreads rating or volume contributes zero to the book ingredients. Previous leaders are the five-cell leading group from the vote-support quality pass. Replacement candidates are compact-ranked cells absent from that previous leading group; stable cases are compact-ranked candidates still present there.
question: With the compact title connection, which up to five cross-source quality candidates outside the previous leader set become the strongest replacement candidates, and which five leaders remain stable across IMDb and book evidence?

context: Now separate the value of cross-source fusion from the compact title connection. Return to the previous cleaned title connection and vote-support quality reading, but keep current market eligibility so the comparison stays in the same business universe. Across the full compact cross-source pool, compare compact-connection rows by the direct score gain over the earlier adjusted-quality reading without rescaling either score. Durable cases are those that already had an earlier adjusted-quality rank.
question: Which five compact-connection candidates are mainly explained by cross-source fusion, and which five would still rank well under the earlier quality reading? Report the largest direct score gains and the most durable cases.

context: Measure recommendation coherence from wording alone first, because weak descriptions were the earliest discoverability concern. Use scikit-learn English-stopword TF-IDF on descriptions with default lowercasing, tokenization, and L2 normalization, keeping terms that appear in at least two titles. Use the whole cleaned catalog as the neighbor universe and evaluate the eight highest cross-source quality candidates. Within each displayed cell, inspect at most the first 80 retained assigned catalog entries in the current assignment order, or all assigned entries when fewer than 80 are available. For each inspected entry, use its ten nearest wording neighbors by cosine similarity without counting the entry itself; order neighbors by similarity descending, and when similarities tie prefer the larger retained catalog index. A niche's wording coherence is average similarity multiplied by one-half plus the share of retrieved neighbors from the same displayed market-category cell. That same-cell percentage uses all retrieved neighbor slots for the inspected entries as the denominator. For multi-market or multi-category neighbor titles, count a hit when the neighbor is attached to the displayed market and displayed cleaned category.
question: Under wording-only similarity, which five cross-source quality candidates have the strongest recommendation coherence and which five look most isolated despite their quality signal? Report wording coherence, same-cell neighbor percentage, and average similarity.

context: Add metadata to the recommendation view instead of using wording alone. Build the similarity text from title, director, cast, every cleaned category attached to the title, every split market attached to the title, and description. Use scikit-learn's default count-vectorizer tokenization with English stopwords, terms appearing in at least two titles, and no more than 30,000 features. For the same quality candidates and per-cell inspection limit, keep excluding the title itself from its neighbor list and score neighbors by raw count-vector dot-product similarity; order neighbors by dot-product similarity descending, and when similarities tie prefer the larger retained catalog index. Metadata coherence is average dot-product similarity multiplied by two factors: first by 0.45 plus the same-category neighbor share expressed as a 0 to 1 fraction, and then by 0.45 plus the same-market neighbor share expressed as a 0 to 1 fraction. Same-category and same-market percentages use all retrieved neighbor slots for the inspected entries as their denominator. They are judged against the displayed niche category and market, with multi-attached neighbor titles counted as hits when they include the displayed value. Neighborhood drift is reported in percentage points as the average of 100 minus the same-category neighbor percentage and 100 minus the same-market neighbor percentage.
question: With metadata-aware similarity, which five quality candidates show the largest improvement in recommendation coherence, and which five drift most in genre or market neighborhood? Report metadata coherence, wording coherence or same-category and same-market percentages as applicable, and the derived improvement or drift.

context: Keep recommendation checks aligned with the same market eligibility and audience-risk compatibility used by the opportunity work. Keep metadata-aware similarity and the same per-cell inspection limit, but restrict neighbor candidates to titles credited to at least one eligible market, not necessarily the candidate's own market, and to titles whose broad-risk value matches the niche's broad-risk share read as 1 when at least half of retained titles in that niche are broad-risk and 0 otherwise. Continue excluding only the catalog entry being scored, not other entries with a matching title key. If fewer than ten neighbors remain after the restriction, use all available neighbors. Compare restricted coherence with the unrestricted metadata-aware reading; loss from the restriction means unrestricted metadata coherence minus restricted coherence.
question: Inside the compliant recommendation pool, which five quality candidates retain strong coherence and which five lose the most compared with the metadata-aware unrestricted view?

context: As a restriction sensitivity check, remove the compliant-pool restriction and compare the result with the current restricted recommendation view. This separates real similarity from lift created by the restriction itself. Report lift as restricted coherence minus unrestricted metadata coherence, and treat a niche as genuinely coherent only when both readings are positive.
question: When the compliant-pool restriction is relaxed, which five niches show the largest artificial lift from the restriction and which five appear genuinely coherent under both recommendation readings?

context: Return to the restricted recommendation view. Add long-running television footprint only for the same eight cross-source quality candidates evaluated in the recommendation checks, and only for those candidates that include shows. Long-running shows are those at or above the 75th percentile of season count among all cleaned television titles. Television-heavy cases are candidates with at least one show. The long-running-show share uses television titles in the niche as its denominator. The television-depth adjustment is that share multiplied by restricted recommendation coherence, so it changes opportunity grades only where season depth affects the portfolio story. Select the largest upgrades by television-depth adjustment descending and the smallest upgrades by that adjustment ascending.
question: Which five television-heavy niches receive the largest opportunity-grade upgrade and which five receive the smallest upgrade once long-running show depth is considered? Report both groups.

context: Move from candidate discovery to a portfolio-ready screen by removing thin market-category cells that are not strong enough for a decision, while still tracking cells that looked attractive earlier. Work from the ten compact cross-source candidates created for the text-risk shortlist, not just the eight cells reviewed in the recommendation checks, and keep that ten-row pool for later opportunity scoring. Join restricted recommendation coherence and television-depth evidence where available; missing restricted coherence counts as zero for screening. Keep cells with at least 20 titles, cross-source score at or above the 55th percentile of that ten-cell table, and restricted recommendation coherence at or above the 45th percentile of the same table after the missing-zero treatment, using linear interpolation for both percentile bars. Earlier high-potential niches are the ten text-risk shortlisted cells carried into the quality checks. Removed historical cases and remaining portfolio candidates are judged by cross-source score and restricted recommendation coherence.
question: After applying the portfolio-ready filter, which five earlier high-potential niches are removed, and which remaining niches become the strongest portfolio candidates? Report the screening bars plus title count, cross-source score, and restricted coherence for each reported niche.

context: Return to the compact cross-source candidate pool before the portfolio filter, but keep the restricted recommendation reading. Measure each excluded niche by its signed distance below the quality, coherence, and title-support bars just used, where a negative shortfall means the bar was exceeded. Recommendation-strong exclusions are judged by restricted coherence and cross-source score.
question: Which five excluded niches still look recommendation-strong in the compact catalog view, and how far below the portfolio bars did they fall?

context: Roll the category lens into broader programming families to stress-test the portfolio discussion, while recomputing the market-family view across all eligible split-market family cells with at least 20 titles. Compare that macro-first table against the ten fine-category cross-source quality winners from the compact title connection, so the rollup is judged by information loss. Preserve Dramas, Comedies, Action & Adventure, Documentaries, and International as their own families; group Romantic and LGBTQ as Romance & Identity; Kids & Family and Anime as Youth & Animation; Crime, Thrillers, Horror, and Mysteries as Crime & Suspense; Stand-Up & Talk and Reality TV as Unscripted & Talk; Classic & Cult and Independent as Specialty Film; Music, Sports Movies, Science & Nature, and Faith & Spirituality as Lifestyle & Factual; British, Korean, and Spanish-Language as Regional TV; all remaining labels fall under Other. At the market-family level, recompute fusion quality from compact IMDb and Goodreads evidence as 68% adjusted IMDb divided by ten, 22% Goodreads rating multiplied by two and divided by ten, and 10% log Goodreads volume scaled by the maximum Goodreads volume in the book table, using the same missing-evidence handling as the compact quality pass. Dilution is the direct fine cross-source score minus the macro fusion quality with no rescaling. Preserved cases must have macro evidence and are selected by macro rank ascending, then dilution ascending; diluted cases are selected by largest positive dilution. Treat the rollup as a comparison view: later opportunity rows keep the displayed fine-category niche name unless the analysis asks for market-family rows.
question: After rolling categories into broader programming families, which five fine-category quality winners are preserved most faithfully, and which five are diluted the most?

context: For an aggregation-order stress test, reverse the category handling order. Start from the full compact fine-category cross-source table, select its top fifteen rows globally, or all rows if fewer than fifteen are available, then roll those selected rows up within each market to market-family cells and average their cross-source scores within each cell. Compare those fine-first market-family cells with the macro-first market-family table recomputed across all eligible market-family cells with at least 20 titles. Join by market and family name, and use zero for the missing side when a family appears in only one order. Sensitivity is the absolute direct score gap between fine-first and macro-first readings. Stable cases are present in both readings with the smallest absolute gap.
question: Which five broader programming families are most sensitive to the order of aggregation, and which five remain stable whether fine categories are selected before or after the rollup?

context: Bring together the earlier packaging pressure, freshness gap, weak text signals, and cross-source quality into a formal opportunity slate. Use the ten-row pool kept during the portfolio screen, including cells that failed one bar. Min-max scale each component within that pool, returning zero for a component if all candidate values are identical. Combine pressure at 30%, new-content gap at 22%, text risk at 18%, and cross-source quality at 30%.
question: Which five niches form the strongest opportunity slate under that combined reading? Report the final score together with the raw pressure, freshness-gap, text-risk, and cross-source quality values behind each row.

context: Account for story-source support and category saturation in the opportunity reading. Keep the same business universe and compare the adjusted ordering with the combined opportunity ordering from the previous step. The five-cell boundary may be stable, so also review the strongest adjusted cases outside the earlier five-cell group and the previous followers that still sit outside the adjusted five-cell group. For adaptation lift, use the existing market-niche adaptation signal when the displayed niche name matches; unmatched family-style names receive zero adaptation lift. For saturation, map each displayed niche to its broader family, count distinct retained catalog entries in the same split-market and broader-family cell from the rolled-up category assignments, then min-max scale that count within the current opportunity pool. The adjusted score keeps 74% of the combined opportunity score, adds 18% of scaled adaptation lift, and subtracts 8% of scaled broad-family title saturation.
question: After adding adaptation support and saturation pressure, which five strongest adjusted followers remain outside the earlier five-cell group, and which five previous followers still fail to enter the adjusted five-cell slate? Report adjusted ranks and scores, with adaptation lift and family title saturation where they explain the adjustment.

context: Return to the middle fine-category quality view while keeping the current decision framework from the adjusted opportunity slate. This isolates the effect of the later cross-source, adaptation, and portfolio choices. Use the adjusted IMDb quality view from the ten text-risk niches with at least three cleaner-title IMDb matches. In this middle view, join the previously carried freshness gap and adaptation signal by the same market and fine-category name; missing joined values contribute zero. Scale each component within that middle-view pool and combine pressure at 30%, new-content gap at 22%, text risk at 18%, vote-support quality at 22%, and adaptation lift at 8%. First check how the current five adjusted-opportunity leaders sit inside the middle-view ranking. For the dependency read, use the full adjusted-opportunity pool from the previous step, exclude cells in the middle-view top five, and report the highest-ranked remaining current candidates by adjusted-opportunity rank.
question: Using the middle fine-category quality view inside the current decision framework, which current leaders still enter the five-cell top group, and which five current candidates depend most on the later quality and rollup choices?

context: Move audience risk away from the teen-inclusive reading and back to stricter format-aware caution. Keep the current displayed market-category cells, quality, and opportunity framework; only replace the audience-risk reading. Movies are risky when rated R or NC-17, and shows are risky when rated TV-MA. Recompute the pressure score on eligible-market cleaned fine-category cells with the same support, weak-description, and risk-weight structure, using cells with at least 20 titles, then match those scores back to the displayed cells. Pressure change is this raw stricter pressure minus the raw pressure value carried in the adjusted opportunity table for the same displayed cell. Missing stricter pressure contributes zero before the subtraction. Add one-fifth of the pressure change to the current opportunity score when judging whether leaders remain strong.
question: With format-specific audience risk, which five opportunity candidates appear to have entered mainly because of the earlier broad risk reading, and which five remain strongest? Report pressure change, format-specific pressure, raw broad pressure, and type-adjusted score where applicable.

context: For a source-sensitivity check, remove book-adaptation lift from the current opportunity reading while keeping format-specific audience risk. This identifies opportunities that are mostly story-source driven by subtracting the same scaled adaptation contribution added to the adjusted opportunity reading. Compare the current type-adjusted ranking with the no-lift top five. Story-source-driven cases are selected from the current type-adjusted ranking after excluding the no-lift top-five cells, taking the highest current type-adjusted ranks first; retained leaders are the no-lift top five. After this check, keep adaptation in the main opportunity view.
question: Without adaptation lift, which five current candidates look most story-source driven, and which five current opportunity leaders remain? Report both groups.

context: Return to the current opportunity reading with adaptation included. Add recommendation coherence and cross-market transferability, using the restricted recommendation behavior and split-market coverage already built. Transferability is the number of distinct split markets attached to the displayed niche's broader family across the full rolled-up category assignment table. Scale restricted recommendation coherence and transferability within the current candidate pool, then combine type-adjusted opportunity score at 68%, recommendation at 20%, and transferability at 12%. For each row, name the component with the largest weighted contribution in that final sum.
question: After adding recommendation coherence and cross-market transferability, which five niches form the final opportunity slate and which component is most responsible for each one? Report final rank, final score, largest component, restricted coherence, and transferability.

context: Return to the wording-only recommendation reading while keeping the current market, category, audience-risk, and opportunity framework. Evaluate the full final pool, not just the reported top five. Recompute only the recommendation component with the wording coherence scale by matching displayed market and niche name to the wording-only table. Any displayed niche absent from that table receives zero wording coherence before the recommendation component is min-max scaled, including family-style names and ordinary fine-category names that were not among the wording-neighbor candidates. Keep the same 68% opportunity and 12% transferability contributions. Bias is current final score minus wording-based score, so positive values indicate dependence on the metadata-aware reading. Well-supported cases have the smallest absolute bias.
question: Under the wording-only recommendation reading, which five final-candidate niches show the largest recommendation-reading bias and which five remain well supported?

context: Return to the middle state that used eligible markets, cleaned fine categories, broad audience risk, and vote-support quality. Exclude the later cross-source fusion, adaptation adjustment, and portfolio-ready filter while applying the current decision logic as closely as possible. Use the middle-state adjusted IMDb quality view and join the previously carried freshness, text-risk, restricted recommendation, and pressure signals by the same market and fine-category name. Missing joined freshness or recommendation values contribute zero. Scale and combine vote-support quality at 36%, new-content gap at 22%, text risk at 18%, restricted recommendation coherence at 14%, and pressure at 10%. Serious middle-state opportunities are the top five by this score. For disappeared current leaders, compare the full current final candidate pool to that middle-state top-five list by the same market and displayed niche name, then report the highest current final ranks that are absent. If a later family-style name does not appear as a fine-category name there, it counts as absent.
question: In that middle-state view, which five niches would still qualify as serious opportunities, and which five current leaders disappear once the later rollup and portfolio filter are removed?

question: Which five brand families have the largest risk-score movement after this low-feedback score adjustment? Report the brand family, prior brand risk score, adjusted brand risk score, score movement, adjusted repaired score, and promoted income share.

context: Hold the adjusted brand-risk non-score pieces fixed, replace only the score input with the restaurant-and-period repair, and compare against the adjusted result.
question: Which five brand families owe the most of their adjusted risk movement to the score adjustment itself? Report the brand family, adjusted risk score, restaurant-and-period risk score under the same non-score settings, and the difference.

context: Discount promoted platform income by 20 percent on orders that are cuisine-relative slow or have the low-feedback adjusted score below 4.0. question: Which five brand families retain the highest experience-adjusted platform value, and which of the three low-feedback risk-movement leaders still appear in that value list? question: Which names show the largest disagreement between the early guardrail and the current brand-family view? Report up to three early-held restaurants that look less concerning now and up to three brand families newly elevated by the current view.

context: Remove only the slow-service part of the experience income penalty and compare current risk ranks with and without it. Mark whether each brand was among the newly elevated names from the disagreement review.
question: Which five brand families change the most in current risk rank when the slow-service penalty is removed from income? Report the brand family, risk rank with the slow penalty, risk rank without the slow penalty, rank change, and whether it was in the newly elevated group.

context: Refine service risk by comparing each order only with orders from the same cuisine and business period. An order is structurally slow when its service minutes are more than one sample standard deviation above that peer group's average. Focus on brands in the top quarter by experience income share.
question: Which five high-income brand families looked slow under the cuisine-relative service view but do not look structurally slow under the cuisine-period service view? Report brand family, experience income share, cuisine-relative slow percent, structural slow percent, slow-risk reduction, and adjusted score.

context: Quantify the peer-group change by taking only the service-risk lens back to the cuisine-relative view and comparing it with the structural service review.
question: Which five brands from the structural service review would lose the most service advantage when judged again by the cuisine-relative view? Report brand family, structural slow percent, cuisine-relative slow percent, service advantage lost, and experience income share.

context: Build current management risk from four sources: original feedback coverage, experience income share, structural service risk, and single-restaurant income concentration. Convert each source to a percentile risk rank, sum the four ranks, and divide by the low-feedback adjusted score. The dominant source is the largest of the four source ranks.
question: Which three brand families have the highest current risk score, and what is the dominant source for each? Report the brand family, current risk score, original missing-feedback percent, experience income share, structural slow percent, single-restaurant income concentration, and dominant source.

question: Which five brand families change risk rank the most under the middle operating mix? Report the brand family, current rank, middle-combination rank, rank change, current risk score, and middle-combination risk score.

context: Apply a stricter observed-evidence score treatment: add ten cuisine-average scores to each restaurant's observed score sum and divide by observed count plus ten. Keep observed order scores as recorded, let only missing orders borrow that restaurant-level result, and leave the current feedback, income, service, and concentration pressure fixed.
question: Which five brand families have the largest current-risk movement after this observed-evidence score treatment? Report the brand family, risk score before this score treatment, risk score after it, score-driven movement, and the newer adjusted score.

context: Test targeted support for restaurants with weak feedback coverage instead of weekend cuisine demand. Apply the same 10 percent ticket reduction only to restaurants whose original missing-feedback percent is above the opening restaurant-level median. Recalculate current experience-adjusted income under this setup.
question: Which five brand families gain or lose the most experience-adjusted income share under targeted support? Report the brand family, current experience income share, targeted-support income share, and income-share change.

context: Set income back to the promoted treatment before experience penalties while keeping the current observed-evidence score and structural-service settings. Rebuild the four-source risk score with that pre-penalty income share and compare it with the current observed-evidence risk ranks.
question: Which five brand families change risk rank the most when income is taken back before experience penalties? Report the brand family, current risk rank, rank under the pre-penalty income, rank change, and income share under the pre-penalty income.

context: Move expansion planning to operating cells defined by cuisine, business period, and brand family. Use observed-evidence experience income from the current risk view rather than the targeted-support counterfactual. Keep cells with at least three orders. The cell opportunity score averages percentile ranks for order count, experience income share, observed-evidence score, inverse structural slow percent, and inverse original missing-feedback percent.
question: Which five cuisine-period-brand cells have the strongest expansion opportunity under this finer operating view? Report cuisine, business period, brand family, order count, opportunity score, experience income share, observed-evidence score, and structural slow percent.

The action score is the cell opportunity score times one plus positive weekend lift divided by 100, times one plus the early cuisine opportunity score, then divided by one plus current brand risk.
question: Which three operating cells are the most actionable expansion choices after combining the early weekend-led cuisine signal with current cell quality and current brand risk? Report cuisine, business period, brand family, action score, early cuisine opportunity score, current cell opportunity score, and current brand risk score.

context: Before committing to cell-level actions, compare their cuisines with the current restaurant-equal cuisine view. Consider every cuisine appearing among eligible actionable cells, not only the displayed choices. The current restaurant-equal support score uses observed-evidence experience income and averages percentile ranks for average restaurant orders, average experience income, average observed-evidence score, inverse average structural slow percent, and inverse average original missing-feedback percent.
question: Which five cuisines from the actionable operating cells lose the most support when the comparison returns to the restaurant-equal view? Report the cuisine, best action score from the finer view, restaurant-equal support score under that view, and support gap.

question: Which five brand families have the largest decision-score swing between the middle score repair and the observed-evidence score treatment? Report the brand family, middle-score decision value, observed-evidence decision value, swing, and original missing-feedback percent.

context: Turn the current brand and cell analysis into a management action list. A brand expands when its best action score is at or above the 75th percentile and its current risk is below the 75th percentile; it reduces when current risk is at or above the 75th percentile and best action score is at or below the median; all others are watched. The final decision score is action-support percentile minus current-risk percentile. Use action support as the driver for expansion examples, the leading risk source for reductions, and the side farther from the midpoint for watched brands. Choose watched brands closest to neutral and reductions with the most negative final scores.
question: Which brand families best represent each management class, and what is the dominant driver for each? Report at most three per class with brand family, class, final decision score, dominant driver, and the relevant driver value.

context: For the closing comparison, rerun the management classes under the middle combination: restaurant-and-period score repair, promoted income before experience penalties, cuisine-relative service risk, and restaurant-equal cuisine support. Keep the current brand-family grouping. A brand's middle support is the strongest restaurant-equal support among the cuisines it participates in. Use the same expand, watch, and reduce threshold inclusions as the final management view, with percentile cutoffs recomputed within this middle combination.
question: Which brand families would receive a different management class under the middle combination, and what mainly explains the difference? Report up to five changed brand families with final class, middle-combination class, final score, middle-combination score, and the main reason for the change.

context: Start with a clean FoodHub order ledger that can support the full analysis. Keep valid numeric ratings, flag nonnumeric ratings as missing feedback, build clean keys for restaurant, cuisine, customer, and day type, and create cost bands from order-cost quartiles: up to the 25th percentile, up to the median, up to the 75th percentile, and above the 75th percentile. For the first business screen, compute an order-level first commission by applying 20% to orders above 20 dollars, 15% to orders above 5 dollars and at most 20 dollars, and zero otherwise. At the restaurant-unit level, first commission means the sum of those order-level first commissions across all orders in the unit; call this summed value commission_first, and do not use average commission for watch-list thresholds, ranking, or reported commission. Treat preparation plus delivery time above 60 minutes as service drag. Use unrounded intermediate values. Report decimal-valued final fields rounded to 4 decimal places, percentages in 0-100 units, default quantile interpolation, and average percentile ranks unless a later step changes the method. Use valid numeric ratings for rating averages unless a later step assigns values to missing ratings. The restaurant unit is the restaurant-name and cuisine combination, and its displayed label is restaurant_name | cuisine_type. Keep units with at least 5 orders. Compute the eligible-unit commission median from unit-level commission_first sums. A unit enters the first watch list when at least 3 of these pressures are true: commission_first at or above that eligible-unit median, missing-feedback rate above the all-order rate, service-drag rate above the all-order rate, and top-customer order share strictly above the eligible-unit median. Use pressure signal labels high_commission, missing_feedback, one_hour_service_drag, and customer_concentration. Sort the first watch list by pressure_count descending, commission_first descending, missing-feedback rate descending, and displayed label ascending as the final tie-breaker.
question: Build the cleaned ledger and lookup tables, then identify the first operating units that combine commercial potential with unclear or weak experience signals. List the top 8 first-watch-list units using the specified ordering, and include the pressure signals that put each unit on the watch list.

context: Compare the first watch list with a fast popularity-led readout. Some units look attractive by volume, commission, or visible ratings but still carry enough missing feedback and service drag to make a simple recommendation unsafe. Build the popularity pool from the 10 eligible units with the most orders, the 10 eligible units with the largest unit-level commission_first sums from Task 1, and the 10 visibly best-rated eligible units among units with at least 20 valid ratings. Within that popularity pool, overstated cases are exactly the units whose Task 1 first-watch-list flag is true. For the uncertainty index, compute average percentile ranks within the popularity pool itself: 35% commission_first percentile, 20% order-count percentile, 20% missing-feedback rate, 15% first service-drag rate, and 10% top-customer share. Sort overstated cases by uncertainty_index descending, commission_first descending, and displayed label ascending.
question: Among the popularity-pool units that are also in the Task 1 first watch list, which up to 6 should be treated as risky, and what Task 1 pressure signals make the recommendation unsafe?

context: Turn the early observation work into an operating decision. Build the relevant unit set from three sources: the Task 1 first watch list, the Task 2 overstated popularity cases, and the 15 eligible units with the largest unit-level commission_first. Reuse Task 1 definitions for commission_first, pressure flags, and the eligible-unit commercial threshold. Quality is clear when a unit has at least 10 valid ratings and its valid-rating average is at least 4.2. Experience is clear only when the missing-feedback, first service-drag, and customer-concentration pressures from Task 1 are all absent. Use decision labels advance, diagnose, and hold. A commercially meaningful unit with clear quality and clear experience advances; a commercially meaningful unit with no more than 2 total Task 1 pressures or clear quality stays under diagnose; all other relevant units are hold. For primary_reason_first, report the first unmet promotion consideration in this priority order: quality_not_clear, feedback_gap, service_drag, customer_concentration, lower_commission; if none are unmet, report balanced. Within each decision group, sort examples by commission_first descending and displayed label ascending.
question: Create the first three-way operating decision for the relevant units. Show the size of each group and the leading 5 examples in each group using the specified ordering, including primary_reason_first for every listed unit.

context: Silent customers may not be neutral, so pressure-test the Task 3 decision with a more cautious feedback assumption. Reuse exactly the Task 3 decision pool, commercial-meaningfulness rule, experience-clear rule, pressure counts, and original decision_first labels. For this temporary sensitivity only, score every missing rating as 3 and compute avg_rating_negative over all orders in the unit. Under the sensitivity assumption, quality is clear if and only if avg_rating_negative is at least 4.0; do not also require at least 10 valid ratings for this temporary quality gate. Do not replace the main valid-rating averages after this task. Reclassify units with the same advance/diagnose/hold rules, using avg_rating_negative for the sensitivity quality gate. A moved unit is one whose sensitivity decision differs from decision_first. For moved units, rating_shift is avg_rating_negative minus the original valid-rating average. Sort moved units by absolute rating_shift descending, commission_first descending, and displayed label ascending.
question: How many units move between Task 3 operating groups when silent feedback is temporarily scored as 3, and which 8 moved units show the largest absolute rating shifts?

context: Check whether the units cleared to move forward actually reach valuable customers. Units allowed to move forward are exactly the Task 3 units with decision_first equal to advance; ignore the Task 4 sensitivity decisions for this task. In the first customer view, value is led by frequency: using all cleaned customers, a customer is high value when order count is at or above the default 90th-percentile order-count cutoff, or when the customer has at least 6 orders and total spend at or above the customer median total spend. Compute the all-order high-value-customer share across the full cleaned ledger. For each advance unit, compute its order share from those high-value customers. A unit has weak reach when its high-value-customer order share is below the all-order share. Sort weak-reach advance units by coverage gap descending, commission_first descending, and displayed label ascending, where coverage gap is all-order high-value-customer share minus the unit share.
question: Among the Task 3 advance units, which up to 6 have weak high-value-customer reach under the first customer view?

context: Build a subsidy-risk pool from units with weak customer reach, overstated popularity cases, and units under diagnosis in the first decision. If a unit lacks a first customer-view coverage result, treat coverage as unproven and set verified high-value-customer share to zero. The main shortfall is the largest adjusted gap across customer coverage, service drag above the all-order rate, missing feedback above the all-order rate, and rating shortfall from 4.2 divided by five. The risk priority combines percentile positions for first commission, customer coverage gap, first service-drag rate, and missing-feedback rate.
question: Which 8 units are in the subsidy-risk pool report, and what is the main shortfall for each reported unit?

context: Revisit the subsidy-risk pool with service measured relative to day type, since weekday and weekend delivery conditions may differ. Use the 90th percentile of total time within each cleaned day type as the slow threshold. A unit's service interpretation changes when its above-average slow-rate flag differs from the one-hour screen.
question: Which up to 8 subsidy-risk units have their service interpretation changed by the day-type relative screen?

context: Use the day-type screen as the current view, while keeping the one-hour screen as a service sensitivity check. A unit is risky when it has a service flag, a customer coverage gap, or unclear quality. Hold customer and quality judgments fixed, compare the risk state under both service flags, and use the slow-rate gap when no unit crosses the boundary.
question: Which 8 units have service-screen sensitivity, and did any cross the subsidy-risk boundary only because the service screen changed?

context: Management often reviews related restaurants at the brand-family level, where one summary row can dilute or amplify concerns seen at individual restaurants. Group names starting with Blue Ribbon, RedFarm, Sushi of Gari, Sarabeth, Five Guys, or Dos Caminos into those families, and let all other names keep their own name. A family can move forward when commission is at or above the family median, at least 10 valid ratings average at least 4.2, day-type relative slow rate is no higher than the all-order rate, and high-value-customer share is at or above the all-order share. Families missing one or more noncommercial gates remain under diagnosis if their commission is meaningful; otherwise they are held. Compared with available restaurant-level decisions, risk is diluted when the family status is more permissive than the most cautious member status and amplified when it is more cautious than the most permissive member status. Families without a member decision may enter the management discussion but should not be counted as diluted or amplified. Keep every family that is not held at this level, plus any family whose status changes because related restaurants are combined.
question: At the brand-family view, which 8 risks are diluted or amplified compared with the restaurant-level decision?

context: A brand-family summary can hide restaurant-level problems, so inspect the same discussion families at the individual restaurant level. For each eligible restaurant, compute the high-value-customer share from its own orders under the first customer view. A restaurant-level problem exists when the unit has a day-type service flag, a missing-feedback pressure, or below-overall high-value-customer share. Count these problem rows even when the family aggregate is already risky, because the goal is to surface hidden commercial exposure.
question: How many single-restaurant problems sit inside the brand-family conclusions, and which 8 carry first-commission exposure?

context: Test a more aggressive tiered commission schedule for the brand-family candidate pool. Use 25% for orders above 20 dollars, 18% for orders above 15 dollars and at most 20 dollars, 12% for orders above 5 dollars and at most 15 dollars, and zero otherwise. Measure priority gain as the first-commission position minus the adjusted-commission position, with ties sharing the same competition position.
question: Under the adjusted commission schedule, which 8 existing brand-family candidates gain commercial priority?

context: Size the first voucher offer for the brand-family discussion pool using frequency-led high-value customers. Target only their orders. Voucher cost is 20% of order cost, protected commission is adjusted commission from targeted orders, subsidy pressure is voucher cost divided by protected commission, and protected-commission share is targeted protected commission divided by all adjusted commission for the brand. Brands without targeted protected commission have undefined subsidy pressure.
question: Which 8 brand-family candidates have weak voucher economics under the first customer view?

context: Check the voucher target set with spend-led customer value. A spend-led high-value customer is in the top spend decile, or has spend at least the 75th percentile and order count at least the customer median. Compare target brands, protected adjusted commission, voucher cost, and subsidy pressure with the frequency-led sizing. Label changes as spend-led additions, removals, shared targets, and untargeted brands.
question: How does the voucher target set change when customer value is led by spend rather than frequency? Report the target counts and 8 target-set changes.

context: Simple average rating is not enough for promotion decisions when some units have few ratings. Replace it with a credibility-adjusted quality view using the global mean of valid ratings as the prior and 20 prior ratings as the smoothing strength. The credibility-adjusted score is the sum of valid rating values plus 20 times the global valid-rating mean, divided by the number of valid ratings plus 20. The review pool combines the existing brand-family discussion with the weak voucher-economics families from the first sizing check. A candidate has credible quality when this score is at least the global valid-rating mean and rating coverage is at or above the pool median. Track whether changed candidates are downgrades or upgrades.
question: Which 8 candidates change quality status under the credibility-adjusted rating view?

context: Test whether the credibility-adjusted quality view is fragile when rating coverage carries extra weight. Use the same candidate pool. The coverage-weighted score is the credibility-adjusted score minus half of the unrated share, where unrated share uses all candidate orders. The pass threshold is the pool median, and each changed case should keep its change direction.
question: Which 8 quality-boundary candidates are sensitive when rating coverage receives extra weight?

context: Judge service timing relative to cuisine and day type, because some cuisine-period combinations naturally take longer. For each order, subtract the mean total time for its cleaned cuisine and day-type combination. Within each combination, an order is residual-slow when this residual is above the 90th percentile. Review the families that moved forward in the brand-family view and also passed the credibility-adjusted quality discussion. Keep residual-service pressure visible even if no family crosses the new risk threshold.
question: Which 8 safe-promotion families show residual-service pressure, and did any become risky under the residual service screen?

context: Compare the residual service screen with the day-type screen for safe-promotion families. A residual-only risk means the residual-slow rate is above the all-order residual-slow rate while the day-type slow rate is not above its all-order rate. Hold quality and customer judgments fixed. If no residual-only risk appears, use the difference between the two slow rates as the sensitivity signal.
question: Which 8 service-risk conclusions are sensitive to using the day-type service screen instead of the residual screen?

context: Move from brand-family averages to brand-by-cuisine units to see detail that a family rollup can hide. A detailed unit is brand family crossed with cuisine, and only units with at least 5 orders are eligible. A detailed unit is high revenue when adjusted commission is at or above the eligible detailed-unit median, and it has service drag when residual-slow rate is above the all-order residual-slow rate. The family average hides that drag only when the corresponding family-level residual-slow rate is not above the all-order rate.
question: Which 8 brand-by-cuisine units combine high adjusted commission with service drag that the family average could hide?

question: Which up to 8 brand-family conclusions need a hidden detail-level exposure note before they can be reported safely?

context: Move from gross adjusted commission to service-penalized net commission. Residual-slow orders keep 90% of their adjusted commission, while other orders keep all adjusted commission. Review detailed units implicated by hidden service drag or unsafe roll-up; when a family needs the detail note, inspect each cuisine detail inside that family. Explain the loss as service drag when residual-slow order share is at least the premium-or-luxury order share; otherwise explain it as high-price exposure. Premium-or-luxury uses the cost-band labels from the cleaned ledger, and loss rate is service penalty loss divided by adjusted commission.
question: Which 8 detailed units lose net commission after the service penalty, and what explains each loss?

Apply the same 10% reduction to day-type slow orders over the detailed loss-review units, then return to the residual service penalty as the main view. Track loss-position change, residual-minus-day-type loss delta, and adjusted commission.
question: How many loss priorities change under the day-type penalty, and which 8 changes should be reviewed?

context: Rebuild customer value only inside quality-trusted detailed units, where broad customer value is less likely to overstate interest in units that are no longer credible. The quality-trusted space contains eligible detailed units whose smoothed detailed rating meets the global valid-rating prior, without carrying over the brand-family coverage gate. Within those orders, a customer is high value if quality-space spend is in the top decile, or if quality-space spend is at least the 75th percentile and quality-space order count is at least the median. The overall share for this customer group uses all detailed-ledger orders, and the unit-level comparison is made on the service-penalty review set.
question: Which 8 detailed units have a positive gap showing that the global customer preference view was overstating demand once customer value is rebuilt inside the quality-trusted space?

context: Classify detailed review units by stability across the frequency-led, spend-led, and quality-space customer views. For each unit, calculate the order share from each customer group and compare it with the corresponding all-order share. A unit is a stable target if all three shares meet or exceed their all-order reference shares, a stable non-target if none do, and definition-sensitive otherwise.
question: Compare the three customer views for the detailed units under review. Which 5 units look stable, and which 5 are definition-sensitive?

context: Isolate the service penalty's effect while holding customer and quality judgments fixed. In the service-penalty review set, compare a pre-penalty priority score built from adjusted commission, credibility-adjusted rating, and quality-space customer share with a penalized score that replaces adjusted commission with service-penalized net commission. A positive score gap means a unit would regain priority without the penalty; a zero gap means the penalty does not change its percentile-priority order.
question: Which 8 detailed units have a priority gap when service penalties are removed while customer and quality judgments remain fixed?

context: Make the quality view more conservative about low ratings. For each detailed unit under review, calculate 3-star share among rated orders. The stricter quality score is the credibility-adjusted score minus 1.5 times that 3-star share, and a unit passes when this score is at or above the median stricter score in the review set. A downgrade occurs when the detailed quality screen passed but this stricter screen fails. If none downgrade, use low-rating pressure for the fallback review.
question: Which 8 promotion candidates face downgrade pressure when low ratings are penalized more heavily, and did any cross the downgrade boundary?

A downgrade is method-driven when the unit passed the middle quality screen, has quality-space customer share at or above the review-set median, and has service-penalized net commission at or above the review-set median. Other downgrades are mixed business weakness. If no formal downgrade occurs, use the quality-method penalty gap to identify pressure cases.
question: Which 8 cases are sensitive to the stricter low-rating quality method rather than weak revenue or customer coverage?

context: Bring voucher cost into net economics after service penalties. Voucher targets are the quality-space high-value customers, and voucher cost is 20% of order cost for their orders. Voucher-adjusted net commission is service-penalized net commission minus targeted voucher cost. A detailed unit passes the positive-after-voucher gate only if voucher-adjusted net commission is positive and the stricter quality screen passes. Units failing either condition are non-passing, even when voucher-adjusted net commission remains positive. When voucher net margin is shown, use voucher-adjusted net commission divided by adjusted commission.
question: After customer-targeted voucher cost, which up to 8 units pass the positive-after-voucher gate, and which 8 fail that gate?

context: Compare the earlier brand-family management view with the current detailed path. The middle management configuration uses brand-family grouping, adjusted commission before service penalties, and credibility-adjusted quality. A family is acceptable there when its brand decision is forward or diagnostic, adjusted commission is at or above the family median, and credible quality passes. Compare only voucher-adjusted detailed review rows, carrying the family-level middle commercial value onto each reviewed detail row. If no reviewed detailed unit is fully excluded by the current path, use the middle-to-current deterioration signal instead.
question: Which 8 reviewed detailed units look materially worse now than they did under the middle management configuration?

context: Run a combined stress check. Add 5 minutes to weekend delivery time before rebuilding residual service, score missing ratings as 3, and let residual-slow orders keep only 80% of adjusted commission. A unit passes when stressed voucher-adjusted net commission is positive and stressed average rating is at or above the median stressed rating in the detailed review set. The stressed average uses all orders after missing ratings receive the temporary score.
question: Which up to 8 voucher-positive units fail only under the combined stress check?

context: Compare the detailed view, the middle management configuration, and the stress check to separate stable recommendations from sensitive ones. A stable recommendation is positive in the detailed view, acceptable in the middle management configuration, and passing under stress. A sensitive recommendation is positive in the detailed view but fails either the middle configuration or the stress check. A middle-only unit is a reviewed detailed unit that is not positive now but was acceptable through its family in the middle configuration; do not add family-only rows outside the detailed review.
question: Which up to 5 recommendations are stable across the detailed, middle-management, and stress views, and which up to 5 are sensitive?

Carry forward whether each unit's brand appeared in the first watch list, first forward group, or first diagnostic group. Label units by the first applicable status in this sequence: stable across all decision views; positive but sensitive; middle-only; first-watch unit with nonpositive voucher-adjusted value; stricter-quality failure; insufficient voucher-adjusted value. question: For 10 reviewed detailed units from the importance view, why did each one enter, improve, weaken, or leave the recommendation set?

context: Use the attribution view to produce a concise strategy across early risk, middle management acceptability, customer-targeted economics, stricter quality, residual service risk, and the combined stress check. question: What is the commercial tradeoff of adopting only the stable core recommendations, and which five units account for the largest opportunity cost?

context: Start with the food-ordering records and prepare a cleaned order table: trim categorical text, preserve missing ratings as a rating-silence signal, convert provided ratings to numeric values, fill the model-ready rating with the median provided rating, keep the first copy of duplicate orders, and anonymize restaurants by sorting cleaned names alphabetically and assigning codes R001, R002, and onward. On the first pass, mark an order as slow when delivery time is in the top quartile of the cleaned table, and mark it as expensive when order cost is in the top quartile. Treat a customer as repeat-exposed when they have at least two orders and their slow-order share meets or exceeds the cleaned-table slow-order share. Build restaurant-cuisine-day pressure rows with at least five orders; every percentage uses that row's order count as the denominator. Keep the ten highest-scoring rows as the early pressure list. The pressure score is the weighted mean of slow-order share, expensive-order share, rating-silence share, and repeat-exposed share with weights 0.32, 0.25, 0.18, and 0.15, divided by the sum of the active weights. Throughout the analysis, compute sums, gaps, ratios, means, correlations, and model errors from unrounded values; report decimal-valued final results rounded to 3 decimal places. Percentages are always on a 0-100 scale, while pressure scores and score gaps stay on the 0-1 weighted-mean scale. When a later question asks for priorities, gaps, losses, sensitivity, or stability, use the requested measure as the ordering signal.

This analysis uses the 2020 Kaggle Machine Learning & Data Science Survey to profile top-earning data scientists. A key challenge is comparing salaries across countries with vastly different costs of living. To normalize, we convert yearly compensation into "McMeal units" — the number of McDonald's combo meals one's salary can buy locally.
Global formatting convention: top lists and ordered comparisons should follow descending order by the reported metric unless a task explicitly asks otherwise. Compute derived quantities such as sums, gaps, ratios, means, or correlations using unrounded values, and report all decimal-valued final results rounded to 3 decimal places.
Data cleaning steps for computing McMeal units:
1. Add a unique respondent identifier to each survey response.
2. Extract the respondent identifier, yearly compensation, and country.
3. Remove respondents with missing yearly compensation.
4. Remove respondents whose country is "Other".
5. The salary is reported as ranges like "$0-999", "1,000-1,999", ..., "> $500,000". Remove dollar signs and greater-than signs. Parse lower and upper bounds from each range string using the hyphen as separator. For the open-ended ">500,000", set upper bound to 1,000,000.
6. Compute the ceiling midpoint of the lower and upper salary bounds.
7. Keep the respondent identifier, compensation range, country, salary bounds, and midpoint salary in the working salary records.
8. Standardize country names to match the cost-of-living dataset.
9. Inner-join with the cost-of-living data using standardized country names to get the McMeal price.
10. Remove country whose McMeal price is 0, causing division issues.
11. Compute McMeal units as the ceiling of midpoint salary divided by the local McMeal price.
12. Keep only the respondent identifier, standardized country, midpoint salary, and computed McMeal-unit count.
Throughout this analysis, compute derived quantities such as sums, gaps, ratios, means, or correlations using unrounded values, and report all decimal-valued final results rounded to 3 decimal places. Report all percentages and percentage-point differences on a 0-100 scale.

This means each factor measures the prevalence of a characteristic across the entire data science community of a country, including respondents for whom the question was not applicable.
Factor definitions (all denominators = NumberOfUsers):
- ManRatio: proportion who selected 'Man' in the gender question
- Lower30yoRatio: proportion aged 18-29 in the age range question
- HigherThanBachelorRatio: proportion with Master's/Doctoral/Professional doctorate in the education level question

- PythonRatio: proportion who selected 'Python' as a programming language in the programming languages used question

- Over1kWorkersRatio: proportion in companies with 1000+ employees in the company size question

- the per-year aggregate of each index is its mean over rows in that year,
- DSI is defined only for years where both annual aggregates are available, so align the rainfall and temperature annual series by year before z-scoring,
- the z-score is computed within that waterbody's own aligned annual series using population standard deviation,
- and yearly aggregations honour whatever window restriction is currently in force.
A larger DSI means a hotter year, a drier year, or both for that waterbody. Compute the DSI series for Aquifer Petrignano.
